TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 26, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of a Transaction(s) between URI and the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management Relative to the Use of the W.
Alton Jones Campus Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees for an Agreement on substantially the terms set forth in the enclosed Term Sheet, by which URI would allow the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (RIDEM) to manage and use portions of the W.
Alton Jones Campus.
Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the proposed Agreement with the RIDEM on substantially the terms outlined in the enclos ed Term Sheet.
This recommendation is based on a thorough review by and with appropriate stakeholders.
Points to Consider: URI has maintained the W.

Alton Jones Campus since 1962, using the campus for research, teaching, and community-oriented activities.
The campus was closed to the public in 2020, because of the COVID pandemic and amidst ongoing financial concerns.
On November 4, 2024, URI posted a Request for Information (RFI) seeking information on potential uses at the W.
Alton Jones campus that would support URI’s mission as a land grant institution, without impeding URI’s research and educational uses of the Property.
In response to this RFI, RIDEM expressed interest in using the Property for purposes that include administrative functions, educational programming, programs and camps (in collaboration with a third party approved by URI), agricultural activities, veterinary care and animal rehabilitation, wildlife and ecological research, and expanding public access to the property.
RIDEM would also invest in critical infrastructure on the campus, including existing buildings and utilities, and the protection of natural resources, including forest and dam management.

Partnering with RIDEM, the chief steward of the state’s natural resources, an agency with substantial experience in managing forested land and water resources throughout Rhode Island, and whose mission is to protect, restore, and promote those resources, allows URI to reopen the W.
Alton Jones Campus with increased protection of its natural resources and with expanded recreational and educational opportunities for the public.

Through this Agreement, URI would maintain use of the Campus for its current education and research needs and maintain the right to expand those uses as necessary. The fundamental structure and assumptions of this agreement are outlined in the attached Term Sheet. Supporting Information: See attached Term Sheet. Proposed Motion of the Board: To recommend approval of an Agreement regarding the use of portions of the W. Alton Jones Campus at 401 Victory Hwy, West Greenwich, RI by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management as presented on substantially the terms in the enclosed Term Sheet, and that any authorized signatory (as defined in the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents) be authorized to negotiate the terms of any documents relating to such transaction on substantially the terms in the enclosure, with any such changes and additional terms as are deemed necessary or appropriate by the authorized signatory.

Alton Jones Campus since 1962 using the campus for research, teaching, and community-oriented activities.
By partnering with RIDEM, the chief steward of the State’s natural resources, an agency with substantial experience in managing forested land and water resources throughout Rhode Island and whose mission is to protect, restore, and promote those resources, URI may, through the assistance and management of RIDEM, reopen the W.

Alton Jones Campus with increased protection of its natural resources and with increased recreational and educational opportunities for the public.
By creating an Agreement(s) for RIDEM to undertake management of portions of the Campus, URI maintains use of the Campus for its education and research needs, while charging RIDEM with stewarding forest and water resources, trails, public access, and environmental education programs at W.
Alton Jones.

Definitions: For purposes of this Term Sheet, Agreement(s) refers to the instrument(s) used for completing the transaction described in this Term Sheet, which may be memorialized in a memorandum of understanding, license, lease, or other form of agreement or agreements.
Campus refers to the entirety of URI’s 2,300 acre W.
Alton Jones campus Property refers to the portion(s) of the Campus to be identified in the Agreement(s) as the responsibility of RIDEM, which Property is generally anticipated to be the Campus less the Reserved Areas, as tentatively depicted in Exhibit A.
Facilities refers to all buildings, structures, infrastructure, improvements, and fixtures on or of the Property Reserved Area(s) refers to all portions of the Campus that URI is reserving for its own use, also tentatively depicted in Exhibit A.
Note that Exhibit A provides only approximate locations and boundaries, and a more precise map will be developed for inclusion in the Agreement(s).

URI’s Reserved Areas are expected to include the below areas, though a comprehensive identification of Reserved Areas shall be negotiated for inclusion in the Agreement(s). - All active research areas - The entirety of the Nettie Marie Jones Nature Preserve, including the Observatory and Nature Preserve Building and the associated open fields - Little Camp - Shared spaces dedicated for URI Facilities administration and/or equipment storage to be determined, possibly within the Main Campus Operations or Woodvale Farm areas URI reserves the use of the Reserved Areas for purposes of URI’s current and future operations, research, education, and other activities.
If at any point in the future, URI requires use of additional portions of the Property for research activities, educational programs, or community events, the parties will negotiate in good faith for such uses, and URI will give RIDEM priority use of such portions of the Property unless unreasonably burdensome to do so.
Whispering Pines refers to the Whispering Pines Conference Center, the approximate area of which is depicted in Exhibit A, and associated buildings.

Whispering Pines shall be reserved for the use of URI or a third party.
RIDEM shall have no responsibilities for maintenance of this area, unless identified through further discussion.
RIDEM will be responsible for coordinating access to Whispering Pines by URI, the Whispering Pines operator, sublessees, and invitees.
URI may request or require that RIDEM and the Whispering Pines operator enter into a cooperation agreement (or similar form of agreement) to ensure harmonious use of potentially shared spaces or Facilities on the Property as well as abutting spaces.
This agreement may allocate certain operations and maintenance responsibilities.
Term: Ten (10) years with the ability to terminate by either party as stipulated in the termination clause further identified below and determined within the Agreement(s).

Occupancy Date: Upon final execution of the Agreement(s), with phased occupancy to be further negotiated.

Base Rent: Base rent is waived in lieu of RIDEM’s commitment to ongoing maintenance of the Property.
Additional Rent: None Security Deposit: None Sublease: RIDEM will be permitted to sublease or license portions of the Property with URI’s prior written consent and, if required, with the approval of the State Properties Committee.

Assignment: Not allowed Responsibility and Liability Generally: Subject to terms, conditions, exceptions, and other details to be worked out between the parties.
URI’s intention is that RIDEM will take full responsibility for the Property and the activities conducted thereon, at RIDEM’s sole cost and expense.
RIDEM’s responsibility will include (without limitation) operating, maintaining, repairing, and improving the Property and Facilities (with URI’s prior written approval, if required by the Agreement(s)), coordinating and overseeing use of the Property and Facilities, and, consistent with Rhode Island law, broadly indemnifying URI for any and all liabilities relating to the Property or Facilities that may arise during the term of or in connection with the Agreement(s).
Access: RIDEM will have access to the Property at all times.
URI retains rights of access to the entire Campus, excepting the interior of the Facilities managed by RIDEM, barring scheduled inspections and emergency access for repairs or other events that require immediate attention.

In addition, subject to terms, conditions, exceptions, and other details to be worked out between the parties, URI intends to reserve certain areas of the W.
Alton Jones Campus for its own use, and URI further intends that RIDEM’s occupancy and use of the Property would to some extent (i) be shared with a third-party operator of the Whispering Pines Conference Center and surrounding area, and (ii) be subject to URI’s continued use and occupancy of the Reserved Areas.
RIDEM would be responsible for managing and coordinating, in consultation with URI and the Whispering Pines operator when appropriate, access to and use of the Property and Facilities by RIDEM, URI, the Whispering Pines operator, sublessees, invitees, and members of the public, with URI to receive priority access and use upon URI’s reasonable request.
Utilities: RIDEM will be responsible for all utility costs for the Property, including any required utility testing.

Page 4 of 5 Maintenance/Repairs/Capital Improvement: RIDEM will be responsible for all maintenance and repairs to the Property, including all Facilities therein, including, but not limited to, exterior landscaping, snow removal, and trash removal.
RIDEM and URI shall establish a schedule for any shared maintenance, which shall include a charge back to the non-performing party.
RIDEM shall not be responsible for maintenance or repairs to the Reserved Areas or Whispering Pines Conference enter, unless otherwise established in the Agreement(s).
RIDEM will be responsible for maintaining the Property and Facilities in good order and condition and for making all necessary repairs and performing all needed capital improvement work (with URI’s prior written approval if required by the Agreement(s)) in compliance with Applicable Laws and at RIDEM’s expense.

The specifics of this responsibility by RIDEM, including specific activities and locations, as well as any shared maintenance, will be determined within the Agreement(s), however the expected Facilities to be maintained by RIDEM include: - All buildings on the Property, including building envelopes, systems, finishes (e.g., carpentry, painting, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, HV AC, windows and glass, flooring, doors and door frames, lighting). - All utility infrastructure including electrical, telecommunications, propane, oil, septic, generators, fire alarms, sprinkler systems, and water wells at the Property. - All trails and primitive roads (gravel or dirt) on the Property, except those within the area identified as Whispering Pines or Reserved Areas unless otherwise established in the Agreement(s). - The dams at Eisenhower Lake and elsewhere throughout the Campus. - All day-to-day maintenance operations including but not limited to lawn mowing, ice and snow removal from walkways and entrances, pest treatments, trash removal, and custodial services on the Property.

Alterations/Construction: RIDEM will be responsible for all alterations, renovations, capital repairs, and other work to meet the needs of their proposed programming.
In addition, RIDEM will be responsible for any required repairs to the Property to meet Applicable Laws or building codes prior to engaging in any of the proposed uses noted above or otherwise noted within the Agreement(s).
All alterations, renovations, capital repairs, or other work not specified as maintenance must be approved by URI prior to commencing the work.
Financing Requirements: None Insurance Requirements: As stipulated and approved by URI’s Risk Management Office.
Hazardous Materials: No hazardous materials have been identified at this time.
Any introduction of hazardous materials to the Property requires prior written approval from URI’s Environmental Health and Safety Office and will be subject to URI’s requirements based on the hazardous materials proposed at the time.

Termination Clause: For Cause: URI may terminate if RIDEM fails to maintain the Property and Facilities in good working order or correct or cure any material breach of terms and conditions of the Agreement(s) within a reasonable cure period to be provided in the Agreement(s).
The Agreement(s) will also provide for termination for convenience under certain circumstances.

Retention of Campus Name: The parties anticipate that the Campus will continue to be named and identified as the “W. Alton Jones Campus of the University of Rhode Island” and will work together to develop appropriate signage and communications identifying RIDEM as the operator of the Property. Governance: URI and DEM will develop a governance structure to manage non program- related campus operations and any capital improvements of the campus, per the terms of the Agreement(s). Pine Swap Lot (Parcel 2): The parties will discuss any potential use, lease, stewardship or fee transfer of the parcel indicated in Exhibit A as “Pine Swamp Lot (Parcel 2). Review of Preliminary FY 2024 Year-End Numbers and FY 2026 Total Budget Request Enclosure Vice Chair Sabitoni introduced Abby Benson, Vice President for Administration and Finance.
Vice President Benson noted that she would be discussing both the FY24 year-end figures and the FY26 Budget request, with an Action Item slated for later in the meeting for approval of the FY26 request based on this presentation.
This presentation can be found in the enclosure.
Vice President Benson noted that the FY24 figures are for Fund 100 only and are pre-audit figures.
Additionally, she noted to the Committee that the percentages on the FY25 Allocation slide as presented in the packet are incorrect, but today’s presentation would be up to date.
Vice President Benson’s presentation included discussion of FY24 budget v. actual figures, variance detail, FY25 budget allocation, and the FY26 operating budget request to the state.
She emphasized that the FY24 surplus was due to a mixture of operational efficiencies, position vacancy savings, and one-time revenue inflows (state reimbursements, for example).

She additionally thanked the State of Rhode Island Office of Management and Budget as well as the State Legislature for their ongoing support of the University.
Upon questions from the Committee, Vice President Benson noted that future revenues are expected to increase, particularly with respect to research, and also through tuition (particularly graduate tuition).
She added that URIFAE funds were embedded in the revenue figures presented here as components of projects, rather than being called out separately.
Assistant Vice President for Financial Strategy and Planning John Poehlmann discussed the FY26 budget submission, with a focus on the assumptions used for developing the budget, including slightly reduced undergraduate enrollment, the University’s continued exclusion from the State’s Promise and Hope Scholarship programs, an anticipated 5% increase in graduate enrollment, and a 3% tuition increase assumption.
Vice President Benson clarified that increases to tuition and fees will be approved by the Board in February and the budget only includes assumptions regarding these items.

AVP Poehlmann also discussed enrollment considerations used for developing the FY26 budget request, including record numbers of applications to the University, FAFSA rollout challenges, and free/reduced tuition programs not only in RI, but also in NY, NJ, and MA.
Associate Vice President for Enrollment Management and Student Success Dean Libutti discussed various free/reduced tuition programs in nearby states.
The Committee suggested the Board receive a presentation at some point in the future on the effect of these programs on the University.
Vice President Benson concluded the presentation with a discussion of the overall strategy and philosophy used with the development of the University’s budget.

The University of Rhode Island is seeking a dedicated vendor to provide routine and emergency utility maintenance a nd repair services for all underground and above-ground utility systems, excluding electrical, located on the Kingston campus.
The Kingston campus consists of 197 buildings totaling over 4 million square feet with miles of underground utility systems.
These systems include steam, water (potable and non-potable), sewage, storm water and natural gas.
An integral understanding of each o f the university's utility systems is necessary for undertaking the scope of work described in Section 3 of this solicitation.
As such, the selected v endor(s) will be required to study and understand the university's utility systems within the first 6 months of the contract's award date.
The selected vendor(s) will be required to provide pipefitter, steamfitter and p lumbing services, along with all construction equipment, excavation services and materials required to perform the necessary task/repair.
Services s hall also include investigation as necessary to ensure proper repair (locating, camera work, etc).

For clarification, the University will continue to utilize the State Master Price Agreement for general plumbing (MPA #40) and steamfitter work (MPA # 199) for repairs and maintenance outside of the scope of utilities.
SECTION 3: SCOPE OF WORK AND REQUIREMENTS General Scope ofWork Vendors submitting proposals in response to this solicitation must demonstrate that they have the capacity to furnish the labor, materials, and equipment necessary for maintaining and repairing underground and above-ground utility systems, including excavation and restoration services where necessary.
Utility systems covered under this service contract will include steam, potable and non-potable water, natural gas, sewer and storm water infrastructure.
All materials used for maintenance and repairs to utility systems must satisfy code requirements and conform with the University's standards for pipe and fittings.
These standards will be provided to the selected vendor(s) upon award ofthis contract.
Most emergency requests from the University are due to a compromised utility main or service line that directly affects its customers.

As such, vendors must demonstrate they have the capacity to respond to a service call within (1) hour ofthe request for emergency service, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
This requirement includes ensuring the availability ofand providing the equipment necessary for responding to the emergency.
Vendors must demonstrate that they and all response personnel possess appropriate licensure and certifications for performing requested/required tasks.
Evidence ofthese credentials must be submitted as part ofthe proposal.
Vendors must demonstrate that they have access to well-maintained equipment, as well as the resources to provide backup equipment in the event ofa breakdown during an emergency or scheduled repair.
Pertinent utility systems information and service requirements: • Steam system operates at 1 00psi 2017-2 Page 9 of20 Revised I 0/05/2020

o Vendor(s) will provide service up to and including PRVs in each building, as well as associated low-pressure piping beyond the PRY as necessary to ensure a proper repair. o The majority of steam pipe is manufactured by "Thermacore" and is of the jacketed insulated HT406 Type.
Vendors must demonstrate that personnel are certified and have the ability to work on this type of system.
URI has since standardized on a Conduit Pipe-in-Pipe system and accepts products manufactured by Thermacore, Rovanco, and Penna-Pipe. o Maintenance and repair services shall includ e all aspects of the system including main and condensate replacement, steam pit maintenance, steam trap maintenance, drip leg repair, v alve replacement, and welding. • Water system operates at up to I 00psi o V endor(s) will provide service up to and including the building backflow preventer and isolation valves.
Backflow repair certification will be required. o Maintenance and repair services will be required for various types ofpiping.
The majority of pipe is ductile, h owever cast iron, transite a nd plastic exist as well. • Natural gas lines are University owned and op erated.

Distribution pressure is 5 psi. o The University participates in the Operator Qualification Program and requires all contractors to be task certified and adhere to the plan requirements. o This contract will require repair and installation of meters, regulators, service lines and mains, including all restoration services as needed. o Vendor(s) must possess the experience and equipment to service plastic, wrapped steel, bare steel, etc. o Vendor(s) will provide system compliance services including annual l eak detection surveys and cathodic protection maintenance and monitoring. • Sewer Conveyance System o This contract will require service ofall mains and services across the campus to the South Kingstown pump station at Peckham farm. o Maintenance and repair services will be required for various types of piping including clay (VC), cast iron, plastic and transite pipe. o Vendor(s) will provide line clearing, root control, repair, and replacement services. • Storm Water System o Vendor(s) will maintain and repair pipe systems and street drains, providing necessary investigative and drain clearing services as needed.

Specific Activities/Tasks In non-emergency situations the contractor will evaluate the requested maintenance/repair tasks and provide cost and procedural estimates for the work prior to commencement ofthe task.
Additional specific tasks the University will be requiring the vendor to perform are as follows: I.
